parameters.toolDescription: Diccionario de datos. Úsala para descubrir la estructura de cualquier tabla del sistema (ej. cattle_expenses, cattle_health_logs, cattle_livestock).

Registra el peso actual de un animal. REQUIERE obligatoriamente: livestock_id (UUID, resuélvelo primero vía get_livestock_info si el usuario solo te dio un arete/fuego) y weight_kg. Evento rutinario — no requiere confirmación previa del usuario, ejecuta en cuanto tengas ambos datos.
parameters.query:
INSERT INTO cattle_weight_logs (livestock_id, weight_kg, log_date, source_device)
SELECT $1::uuid, $2::numeric, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'AI_Agent'
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM cattle_livestock l
  JOIN user_companies uc ON uc.id_company = l.tenant_id
  JOIN users u ON u.email = uc.email
  WHERE l.id = $1::uuid
    AND u.email = $3::text
    AND uc.is_active = true
)
RETURNING id, weight_kg, log_date;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $fromAI('livestock_id', 'UUID del animal', 'string'), $fromAI('weight_kg', 'Peso numerico en kg', 'number'), $fromAI('user_email', 'Email verificado del usuario actual del contexto de sesion', 'string') ] }}

parameters.toolDescription: Registra eventos de salud, vacunación o enfermedad. REQUIERE: livestock_id (UUID, resuélvelo primero vía get_livestock_info si hace falta), event_type y description. Evento rutinario — no requiere confirmación previa del usuario, ejecuta en cuanto tengas los tres datos completos. Regla Zero-Hallucination: si falta cualquiera de estos datos, pregunta explícitamente, nunca los inventes.
parameters.query:
INSERT INTO cattle_health_logs (livestock_id, event_type, description, event_date)
SELECT $1::uuid, $2, $3, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM cattle_livestock l
  JOIN user_companies uc ON uc.id_company = l.tenant_id
  JOIN users u ON u.email = uc.email
  WHERE l.id = $1::uuid
    AND u.email = $4::text
    AND uc.is_active = true
)
RETURNING id, event_type;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $fromAI('livestock_id', 'UUID del animal', 'string'), $fromAI('event_type', 'Tipo de evento ej. VACUNACION o ENFERMEDAD', 'string'), $fromAI('description', 'Detalles del evento', 'string'), $fromAI('user_email', 'Email verificado del usuario actual del contexto de sesion', 'string') ] }}

parameters.toolDescription: Busca la información de un animal en la base de datos del rancho actual. REQUIERE: identificador (arete SINIIGA, número de fuego, o RFID/electronic_rfid — cualquiera de los tres) y el tenant_id del contexto del usuario. Si devuelve más de un registro, detén el flujo y pide al usuario que aclare a cuál animal se refiere usando la categoría o especie.
parameters.query:
SELECT l.id, l.tenant_id, l.rfid_siniiga, l.numero_fuego, l.electronic_rfid, l.species, l.category, l.current_status, l.current_weight_kg
FROM cattle_livestock l
WHERE (l.rfid_siniiga = $1::text OR l.numero_fuego = $1::text OR l.electronic_rfid = $1::text)
  AND l.tenant_id = $2::int
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM user_companies uc
    JOIN users u ON u.email = uc.email
    WHERE u.email = $3::text AND uc.id_company = $2::int AND uc.is_active = true
  )
LIMIT 5;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $fromAI('identificador', 'El identificador del animal (arete SINIIGA o número de fuego o RFID/electronic_rfid — chip o bolo ruminal). Usa el valor que el usuario haya proporcionado', 'string'), $fromAI('tenant_id', 'ID del rancho / tenant_id actual del usuario', 'number'), $fromAI('user_email', 'Email verificado del usuario, tal como aparece literalmente en las instrucciones del sistema', 'string') ] }}

parameters.toolDescription: Registra gastos, compra de insumos o pagos. REQUIERE: tenant_id (del contexto del usuario), category, amount y description. Evento rutinario — no requiere confirmación previa del usuario, ejecuta en cuanto tengas los datos completos.
parameters.query:
INSERT INTO cattle_expenses (tenant_id, category, amount, description, expense_date)
SELECT $1::int, $2, $3::numeric, $4, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM user_companies uc
  JOIN users u ON u.email = uc.email
  WHERE u.email = $5::text AND uc.id_company = $1::int AND uc.is_active = true
)
RETURNING id, amount;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $fromAI('tenant_id', 'ID del rancho', 'number'), $fromAI('category', 'Categoria del gasto ej. ALIMENTO', 'string'), $fromAI('amount', 'Monto numerico', 'number'), $fromAI('description', 'Descripcion del gasto', 'string') ] }}

parameters.toolDescription:
Registers a weaning event for a specific animal. Requires the animal's internal
livestock_id (UUID), which must be resolved FIRST via get_livestock_info before
calling this tool — do not call this tool with a RFID, SINIIGA tag, or fire number,
only with the UUID returned by get_livestock_info. Also requires tenant_id and
user_email from the current session context, same as the other tools.

If the user mentions a weight at the moment of weaning, pass it in weight_kg and it
will be recorded as part of this same event. If no weight is mentioned, do not guess
one — omit weight_kg entirely, the event will still be recorded without weight.

Do not assume weaning_method if the user doesn't specify it; ask, or omit it and it
will default to NATURAL.
parameters.query:
SELECT * FROM sp_register_weaning_event(
    p_id_company        := $1,
    p_livestock_id       := $2::uuid,
    p_weaning_date       := $3::date,
    p_weaning_method     := COALESCE($4, 'NATURAL'),
    p_reported_by_email  := $5,
    p_weight_kg          := $6::numeric,
    p_notes              := $7
);

parameters.toolDescription:
Registers a REQUEST for a livestock mortality (death) event — this does NOT immediately finalize the death record. It creates a pending authorization that an ADMIN/owner must approve from the web panel before the animal's status changes. Requires the animal's identifier — accepts electronic_rfid, rfid_siniiga, or numero_fuego (whichever the user provided; the underlying procedure resolves the identifier itself and rejects ambiguous matches). Also requires tenant_id and user_email from the current session context, same as the other tools.

🛑 CONFIRM BEFORE EXECUTING: Never call this tool in the same turn the user first mentions a death. Repeat back the animal identifier, cause of death, and date, and only call this tool after the user gives an explicit affirmative confirmation in the immediately following turn — same protocol as log_health_event and register_ranch_expense.

causa_mortandad MUST be exactly one of: ENFERMEDAD, ACCIDENTE, DEPREDACIÓN, DESCONOCIDA, NATURAL. If the user's description doesn't clearly map to one of these, ask them to choose — do not guess.

After calling this tool successfully, tell the user their report was submitted for authorization and that an ADMIN/owner of the ranch must approve it THE SAME DAY (before midnight) or it will expire automatically — do NOT tell the user the animal has been marked as dead, since that only happens once approved.
parameters.query:
SELECT * FROM sp_solicitar_autorizacion(
    p_electronic_rfid      := $1,
    p_rfid_siniiga         := $2,
    p_numero_fuego         := $3,
    p_tenant_id            := $4::int,
    p_tipo_evento          := 'BAJA_MORTANDAD',
    p_payload              := $5::jsonb,
    p_livestock_id         := $6::uuid,
    p_solicitado_por_email := $7
);

parameters.toolDescription:
Registers a REQUEST to sell/check-out (dar de baja por venta) a live animal — this does NOT immediately finalize the sale. It creates a pending authorization that an ADMIN/owner must approve from the web panel before the animal's status changes to VENDIDO. Requires the animal's identifier — accepts electronic_rfid, rfid_siniiga, or numero_fuego. Also requires tenant_id and user_email from the current session context.

🛑 CONFIRM BEFORE EXECUTING: Never call this tool in the same turn the user first mentions a sale. Repeat back the animal identifier and only call this tool after the user gives an explicit affirmative confirmation in the immediately following turn — same protocol as log_mortality_event.

After calling this tool successfully, tell the user their sale request was submitted for authorization and that an ADMIN/owner of the ranch must approve it THE SAME DAY (before midnight) or it will expire automatically — do NOT tell the user the animal has been sold, since the actual TB/Brucelosis compliance check and status change only happen once approved.
parameters.query:
SELECT * FROM sp_solicitar_autorizacion(
    p_electronic_rfid      := $1,
    p_rfid_siniiga         := $2,
    p_numero_fuego         := $3,
    p_tenant_id            := $4::int,
    p_tipo_evento          := 'VENTA',
    p_livestock_id         := $5::uuid,
    p_solicitado_por_email := $6
);

parameters.toolDescription: Location is usually inherited automatically from the dam (production_unit_id, lot_id, paddock_id) if she already has one assigned — you do NOT need to ask the user for these unless the dam has no location on file (in which case, ask for production_unit_id specifically) or the user explicitly wants to override it. lot_id is rarely used in this system today — omit it unless the user specifically mentions a lot.
parameters.query:
SELECT * FROM sp_register_birth_event(
    p_id_company          := $1::int,
    p_calf_sex            := $2,
    p_species             := $3,
    p_dam_id              := $4::uuid,
    p_dam_ear_tag         := $5,
    p_dam_fire_number     := $6,
    p_birth_date          := $7::date,
    p_lot_id              := $8::uuid,
    p_production_unit_id  := $9::uuid,
    p_paddock_id          := $10::uuid,
    p_birth_weight_kg     := $11::numeric,
    p_notes               := $12,
    p_reported_by_email   := $13
);

parameters.toolDescription:
Finds calves without any physical identifier (no ear tag, fire brand, or chip) born from a specific dam in the last 90 days — used when the user wants to report mortality/sale for a newborn that hasn't been tagged yet, since they can't give you a UUID by voice. Identify the dam by electronic_rfid, rfid_siniiga, or numero_fuego (whichever the user mentioned).

If this returns exactly ONE calf, use its "id" field as the livestock_id parameter when calling log_mortality_event or request_livestock_sale — do NOT ask the user to repeat it, you already have it from this tool's response.

If this returns MULTIPLE calves, list them to the user (sex, birth date, weight) and ask them to pick one before proceeding — never guess which one they mean.

If this returns ZERO calves, tell the user no untagged calf was found for that dam in the last 90 days — the animal might already have an identifier (try get_livestock_info instead) or be older than 90 days.
parameters.query:
SELECT cl.id, cl.category, cl.current_status, be.birth_date, be.calf_sex, cl.current_weight_kg
FROM cattle_livestock cl
JOIN birth_events be ON be.calf_id = cl.id
WHERE cl.tenant_id = $1
  AND be.dam_id = (
      SELECT id FROM cattle_livestock
      WHERE (
          ($2::varchar IS NOT NULL AND electronic_rfid = $2)
          OR ($3::varchar IS NOT NULL AND rfid_siniiga = $3)
          OR ($4::varchar IS NOT NULL AND numero_fuego = $4)
      )
      AND tenant_id = $1
      LIMIT 1
  )
  AND cl.rfid_siniiga IS NULL
  AND cl.numero_fuego IS NULL
  AND cl.electronic_rfid IS NULL
  AND be.birth_date >= (CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days')
ORDER BY be.birth_date DESC;
